title: Container, postmaster and kernel
caption: The container runtime starts a root entrypoint that hands over to the postgres user, and the postmaster then asks the Linux kernel for shared memory, semaphores, sockets and file caching.

title: From docker run to docker stop
caption: Follow the numbers: the entrypoint starts as root, prepares the data folder, steps down to postgres, runs initdb once, then execs the real server, which later gets SIGINT for a fast shutdown.

badges.meaning: docker run starts docker-entrypoint.sh as root (uid 0)
The script creates PGDATA, sets mode 700 and chowns it to postgres
gosu postgres re-runs the script as uid 999 so the server is never root
On an empty PGDATA (no PG_VERSION) initdb creates the cluster
A temporary socket-only server runs /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d files, then pg_ctl stops it
exec postgres replaces the shell, so postgres is PID 1
Startup checks refuse root, require mode 0700 or 0750, and ask the kernel for shared memory, semaphores and sockets
docker stop sends SIGINT, which the postmaster treats as a fast shutdown

title: Layout of the postgres image
caption: The image keeps data in a VOLUME under /var/lib/postgresql, a socket directory, an init-scripts folder and a small /dev/shm, while the kernel supplies stop signals and two kinds of shared memory.
